operations.gives: Rise, set and transit in a window
How much is lit, and the phase's name, at an instant
The next of each of the four main phases after an instant

fields.startUtc: The window's start, ISO 8601 with Z. For nextPhases, midnight UTC.
fields.windowInHours: The window's length: 24 in every case here. More than 0 and at most 48.
fields.instantUtc: An instant, ISO 8601 with Z, read as UT1
fields.riseUtc: The first moment in the window the moon's top edge reaches the horizon, seen from the place (with parallax) and with 34′ of refraction. null if it doesn't happen in the window. USNO gives the minute.
fields.transitUtc: The first moment in the window the moon crosses the meridian. Left out when it stays down all window.
fields.isAlwaysUp: true when the moon is up for the whole window
fields.isAlwaysDown: true when it's down for the whole window
fields.illuminationFraction: 0 to 1, the part of the face that's lit, seen from the Earth's centre
fields.phaseAngleInDegrees: The Sun–Moon–Earth angle: 0 at full, 180 at new
fields.phaseName: From the moon's elongation, its ecliptic longitude minus the sun's, in eight 45° bands each centred on its phase: new within 22.5° of 0, then waxingCrescent, firstQuarter (centred on 90), waxingGibbous, full (180), waningGibbous, lastQuarter (270) and waningCrescent. Instants within 0.5° of a band's edge aren't cases.
fields.newMoonUtc: The first new moon from the start
fields.firstQuarterUtc: The first first quarter from the start
fields.fullMoonUtc: The first full moon from the start
fields.lastQuarterUtc: The first last quarter from the start
